primary_native_comparison.note: All macro/micro/keyframe/rejection counters agree. Entry and final runs use CPUs 184-191; the earlier excellent baseline uses CPUs 80-87 on the same node. Each is one native sample; old binaries were not rerun.

same_node_phase_comparison.note: Fixed-chart primal/tangent transforms are now ordinary actions instead of directional actions with a zero chart direction. Ordinary call counts therefore rise while directional work falls. Nested clocks overlap and are not additive.

implemented: Left/Right/Both overlap-adjoint requests compute only consumed cotangents. Left requests use exact scalar cross-Gram symmetry, not duplicated kernels.
Origin transport curvature, its mixed CI cotangent and its transpose directional forcing share one factor-tile sweep.
The transpose forcing reuses the accepted tile seeds through a directional exterior adjoint; no independent overlap-direction sweep remains in curvature.
One shared W lambda vector; W c and W q are generated only for the current tile. No worker copies of large panels, product images or integrals.
COV factor panels share one 8 MiB allowance. At width 64, their payload is at most 7096320 bytes for 924/924 strings, plus required small outputs and the shared support vector.

Broad complete product support retains the faster one-body-moment order. Its three shared product images must fit the existing 64 MiB overlap allowance; their dead storage is reused. Larger or restricted support uses the exact bounded factor order.
Keyframe transport uses single-sided pullbacks. Its distinct finite-chart calls have not all been fused into one sweep.

verification.coverage: Independent occupied-minor finite differences; single-side versus complete adjoints; fused versus separate contractions; transpose duality; dense and sparse nonclosed selections; equal, unequal and empty-beta spin carriers; 1/4-thread row scatters; one-column/wider budgets; multistate transport; F2 HAO/OEO.
